justifications.functional_suitability: Catalog & Search Service with Elasticsearch covers R-01 for catalogue items, and Circulation Engine, Fine & Fee Manager and Notification Dispatcher cover circulation. Gaps: no explicit digital-item storage or access, and no reporting component for Library Administrators.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Elasticsearch Cluster backs search, Local Availability Cache (BigCache, <5ms) serves lookups, and Indexing Worker updates indices asynchronously. Redis-backed Rate Limiting, the Message Broker and HPA metrics add scaling. No explicit p99 <800 ms budget or load-test mechanism.
justifications.compatibility: Standard protocols are used: OIDC with the Identity Provider, REST over mTLS to Payment Gateway and Notification Service, OTLP to the Observability Platform, gRPC internally. Inconsistencies: the AMQP/MQTT link to Notification Service and the Catalog service authenticating via IdP. No library standards such as MARC or Z39.50.
justifications.usability: Frontend Container (React SPA) with Catalog UI and Circulation UI components serves patrons, librarians and admins, with localized templates in Template Renderer. Gaps: no dedicated admin/reporting UI, no accessibility or responsive-design mechanism beyond a mention, and no digital-item access.
justifications.reliability: PostgreSQL (EU Instance) has primary-replica streaming, Dispatch Worker retries with DLQ, the outbox pattern, and the Local Buffer Manager (SQLite WAL) buffers audit events. Gaps: no multi-instance or failover for Elasticsearch or gateway, no backup/DR, no circuit breakers, and the in-memory cache is volatile.
justifications.security: Strong layered controls: WAF & Threat Protection, JWT Validator, Access Control (ACL), PKCE in Routing & Auth Module, mTLS everywhere, HashiCorp Vault, TDE, and hash-chained immutable audit via Event Normalizer and Compliance Storage Writer with RBAC Compliance Query Service. EU-hosted components support residency.
justifications.maintainability: Clear modular decomposition into separate containers and components with defined responsibilities, gRPC contracts, and the Telemetry Exporter and correlation IDs in API Client Service. Weaknesses: polyglot stack (Node, Go, Java, Python), inconsistent model naming, duplicated components, and the Compliance Officers actor missing from the context.
justifications.portability: Containerized services, Kubernetes HPA hints, and replaceable brokers (RabbitMQ/Kafka) and Vault help. EU-only residency is respected via the EU CDN and PostgreSQL (EU Instance). Gaps: no explicit deployment model, no IaC, and no cloud-vendor abstraction.

sensitivity_points: Gateway WAF and JWT overhead per request
Indexing load competes with query load
Event delivery path to indexer undefined
PERF-02.justification: Indexing worker consumes change events, plausibly meeting the 5-minute target. The event source and broker are unspecified, and no isolation of indexing from query load is shown. Plausible but unproven.

sensitivity_points: Replica count and failover time unspecified
AVAIL-01.justification: Elasticsearch is called a cluster, but replicas and failover are not specified. PostgreSQL has primary-replica streaming without automated failover. Circulation is isolated from search, and ACID persistence protects loans, but the 1-minute recovery is unsubstantiated.

sensitivity_points: Gateway itself may be a single point of failure
Token and session handling is stateless
tradeoffs: CDN static hosting simplicity versus offline capability
AVAIL-02.justification: The SPA is served from a CDN, so a portal instance failure is largely moot. The gateway has load balancing, but its redundancy is not stated. Loan transactions are persisted server-side. Reasonably covered but not explicit.

sensitivity_points: No provider integration or adapter component exists
Catalogue ingestion path for digital items missing
tradeoffs: Single service simplicity versus extension isolation
MOD-01.justification: There is no integration or adapter component for external e-book providers. Changes would likely touch the Catalog service workers, and no plugin or anti-corruption layer confines them to one component.

sensitivity_points: No rules engine or configuration store shown
tradeoffs: Hardcoded rules simplicity versus runtime flexibility
MOD-02.justification: Loan rules live in the Circulation Engine with no configurable rules or policy component. Per-library rules would probably require code changes and redeployment, so the runtime configuration requirement is unmet.

sensitivity_points: Kafka, Elasticsearch and cache region placement unspecified
tradeoffs: Managed external services versus residency control
SEC-01.justification: Context states EU-hosted external systems and an EU PostgreSQL instance and CDN. No technical enforcement such as region policies or telemetry scrubbing is shown, and Elasticsearch and broker locations are not stated. Residency is by declaration, not by design.

sensitivity_points: Object-level ownership check not located in the service
Denied attempts are not clearly routed to audit
tradeoffs: Gateway-level ACL versus fine-grained service authorization
SEC-02.justification: JWT validation and ACLs exist at the gateway, and an immutable audit log exists. But object-level patron ownership checks are not modelled in the Circulation service, and denied-access logging flow is not defined. Partial coverage.
